slide.text: FCT needs stronger title and oversight continuity
In the FCT, land administration sits at the center of public trust, mass-housing title continuity, document regularisation, and capital-region investment confidence.

text.p: The FCT operates in a high-visibility land-governance environment where title records, statutory rights, regularisation workflows, and mass-housing obligations all carry outsized public and investor importance.

When parcel data, review queues, field evidence, and legal progression are fragmented, leadership loses visibility into where cases are delayed, where trust is weakened, and where oversight risk is growing.

p.strong: This makes the procurement case fundamentally about informed decisions, auditable continuity, and more credible land administration at capital scale.

tr.td: Why it matters in FCT procurement terms
Large-scale title issuance and beneficiary workflows require clearer record discipline, queue visibility, and public confidence.
Document re-commencement and regularisation efforts need stronger workflow traceability and coordination between desks.
Reviewed terms, verification activity, and right-of-occupancy controls require auditable progression and better exception handling.
FCT land decisions signal governance quality to residents, developers, lenders, and broader investment audiences.

slide.text: For the FCT, procurement value lies in better-informed land decisions, cleaner title continuity, and stronger public confidence in how high-value records move through the system.
